name: How much should I budget for permits and fees in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget for permits, plan check, and city fees when building a new house in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How much should I budget for permits, plan check, and city fees when building a new house in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permit and city fees in Los Angeles can be a major part of the budget, and they are often underestimated because they are not as visible as framing or finishes. The total depends on the project valuation, lot conditions, scope of work, and whether extra reviews are required for grading, utilities, drainage, or hillside issues. A practical approach is to treat permits, plan check, and related soft costs as their own budget bucket rather than folding them into construction. Ask your builder or designer for an early estimate that separates city fees from consultant fees, since architecture, engineering, surveying, and soils work can add substantially to the total. If you are comparing project bids, make sure each proposal uses the same assumptions for permit scope; otherwise the lower bid may simply be missing important costs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Los Angeles permit and city fees can add tens of thousands of dollars to a new home project, and the total depends on valuation, scope, site conditions, and required reviews. Some projects also need grading, utility, or special inspection fees. The safest budget is a separate contingency for soft costs.
